title: Ramanuja on the temple tower
hook: a teacher gives him a secret mantra; he climbs the temple tower and shouts it to the town
carry: the whole world is God's body
tomorrow: The gopis and the learned messenger

segments.voice: Yesterday: Madhva's Dvaita, the Krishna in the ballast clay. Your line: dvaita, God, souls and world are truly two. Today, a third answer, from a teacher who came before Madhva.

A young scholar named Ramanuja walks, tradition says, eighteen times to the house of an old teacher, asking for a sacred mantra. South India, around nine hundred years ago. Seventeen times he's turned away. The eighteenth time, the teacher gives it, with a warning: keep this secret. Tell no one, or you'll go to hell. Ramanuja walks straight to the temple, climbs the tall gateway tower, and calls the mantra out to everyone in the street below. The teacher is furious. Ramanuja says: if I go to hell and all these people are saved, I'll gladly go.
screen: `EIGHTEEN WALKS TO A TEACHER.` → `KEEP THIS SECRET.` → `SHOUTED FROM THE TEMPLE TOWER.`

segments.voice: The teacher, the story goes, embraced him. Ramanuja became the great teacher of the Sri Vaishnava tradition, centered at the temple of Srirangam, and he gave Vedanta a third answer. Not Shankara's not two. Not quite Madhva's two, which came about a century later. His school is called Vishishtadvaita: not two, but qualified. One reality, with real distinctions inside it. His picture is the body and the soul. You live in your body and guide it from inside. The body is real, not a snake on a rope. But it isn't independent either. It's yours. For Ramanuja, the whole universe, every soul and every grain of matter, is the body of God. And God, Vishnu, Narayana, is the soul of it all. He found this in the Upanishads, where the sage Yajnavalkya describes the inner controller. Paraphrased: the one who dwells in the earth, yet is other than the earth, whom the earth does not know, whose body the earth is, who guides the earth from within: that is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. For Ramanuja, you're really you, forever. God is really God. And yet God is closer to you than your own body is. That's why his tradition sees love and surrender to God as the path. The freed soul doesn't vanish into God. It enjoys God, as God's own. So for Ramanuja's followers the river, the stranger on the bus, your own hands, aren't a trick. The whole world is God's body.
screen: `VISHISHTADVAITA: QUALIFIED NOT-TWO.` · `GOD IS THE SOUL OF IT ALL.` · `THE INNER CONTROLLER.` · `REALLY YOU, REALLY GOD, VERY NEAR.` · then, large: `THE WHOLE WORLD IS GOD'S BODY.`

segments.voice: Feel your body from the inside: your hands, your chest rising, the weight of your legs, really yours. Then try Ramanuja's picture: the room, the city, the trees, the people you love, all one great body, with a life at its center that lives in you too. If you pray, rest in that nearness; if not, feel the body and the room, and breathe.
Vishishtadvaita, not two but qualified. One reality: the world and souls are God's body, God is their inner self, and the soul stays itself, loving God.
Your line: the whole world is God's body. Really you, really God, and very near. That's two eighty-nine.

howItsDone: Sri Vaishnavas, followers of Ramanuja, worship Vishnu with Lakshmi, especially at temples like Srirangam, recite the Alvars' Tamil hymns alongside Sanskrit texts, and practice prapatti, surrender to God, as the heart of the path.

original.note: Sanskrit: vishishta (qualified, distinguished) + advaita (not two): Ramanuja's school.

trapdoor: what you thought: Hindu philosophy has two options, one or two.
what it means: Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita says one reality, God, with souls and world as God's real body.

what a scholar hears: Ramanuja (traditionally 1017–1137) grounds the body-soul relation (śarīra-śarīri-bhāva) in the Antaryami Brahmana, Brihadaranyaka 3.7; the 'secret mantra' in the tower story is usually identified as the eight-syllable Narayana mantra.
